newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT BUSINESS PICKED UP IN 2ND QUARTER.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT BUSINESS PICKED UP IN 2ND QUARTER.

text.p: Dutch paper and office equipment group Koninklijke KNP BT said on Thursday its business had picked up in the second quarter of 1997 after a slow start.
"The year has begun a bit sluggishly, but later we have found some momentum," chief financial officer Rob Bonnier told a news conference on the company's first-half results.

KNP BT repeated that it expected a substantial increase in full-year profits, compared with 1996's 231 million guilders. But Bonnier said that the fourth quarter would be very important for the full-year results as many orders would be delivered by the end of the year.
Bonnier said the KNP BT Distribution division, which includes majority-owned BT Office Products in the U.S., had very good prospects given its order position.
In this sector, orders for graphics and information systems were now at the same level as last year thanks to a recovery in the second quarter, and in Asia they were higher than last year.

KNP Packaging saw good volume growth in the first half of 1997 but this was partly offset because of rising raw material prices. Margins were seen recovering here in the second half of the year due to increases of selling prices.
KNP's paper production division KNP Leykam managed to crawl out of the red in the first half of this year, with operating profits of 22 million guilders.
But despite healthy volume growth in this business, margins are still low here and KNP BT does not expect KNP Leykam's results to change substantially in the second half of 1997.

KNP BT previously announced it would raise its paper prices in September. Bonnier said the price rises for paper could be different from country to country but added a price hike was absolutely necessary.

"There is a clear feeling in the market that (paper) prices can go up and also have to go up," Bonnier said. He said the price rise was vital to compensate for previous increases in raw material prices.
KNP Leykam's giant new production unit in the Austrian town of Gratkorn is expected to come on stream in November.
The previously announced reorganisation at KNP Leykam, which includes cutting 1,000 jobs in several countries, is eventually expected to cut costs by about 100 million guilders per year.
